instruction: Turn off automatic screen locking on my Ubuntu system to prevent the screen from locking when idle.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling automatic screen locking. Setup enables lock-enabled (true), agent must disable it (false). Uses existing vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric. Verified: gsettings returns 'false\n' when disabled.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: vm_command_line executes 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled' which directly queries the GNOME screen lock setting
Metric logic is correct: exact_match performs strict string comparison appropriate for boolean settings
Expected value is correct: 'false\n' matches the actual gsettings output format (verified in metadata)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the single requirement (disable automatic screen locking)
Data flow is correct: getter extracts lock-enabled value, metric compares against expected 'false\n'
Runtime feasibility: gsettings command works on Ubuntu/GNOME systems, no UI state dependencies, no postconfig needed
No edge case issues: handles output format correctly including newline character
